studies.label: Study 2 (AI dependence manipulation, AUT with ChatGPT)

counts_source.quote:
A total of 132 university students (including graduate students; 51 males,
81 females) were recruited and randomly assigned to either the high-dependence group
(n = 66) or the low-dependence group (n = 66).

arms.name: High AI dependence
arms.description: During priming, participants had to use ChatGPT answers for calculation, summarisation, and translation and were told AI answers were optimal. During the AUT, they used ChatGPT and were instructed to adopt its creative solutions directly (PDF pp. 5-6, Section 3.2).

arms.name: Low AI dependence
arms.description: During priming, participants completed the same tasks independently without external tools. During the AUT, they used ChatGPT as a supplementary reference and were instructed to complete final solutions independently (PDF pp. 5-6, Section 3.2).

studies.task: Generate as many innovative uses as possible for a tennis racket and a water pipe in an Alternative Uses Task framed as a creative competition.

estimates.outcome: AUT creativity index (Consensual Assessment Technique, mean of three raters)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Three psychology graduate students, trained in a calibration session and blind to condition, rated novelty, appropriateness, and fluency on seven-point Likert scales. The mean of the three raters’ scores was the creativity index. The paper does not fully describe aggregation across dimensions, ideas, or the two AUT objects (PDF p. 6, Section 3.2, Measures).

stats.difference_is: Printed total effect c of High AI dependence versus Low AI dependence (treatment minus control), as reported in the mediation paragraph; not the mediator-adjusted direct effect and not calculated from the means.

estimates.notes: The eligible full-sample contrast is the same in Table 2 and the total-effect statement: High AI dependence is treatment and Low AI dependence is control, following the screening form. The positive printed t and Cohen’s d describe Low AI dependence minus High AI dependence, opposite to treatment minus control; their printed signs are retained. The printed total effect c is retained as the overall treatment contrast already represented in this record, not as an additional mediation estimate. The direct effect adjusted for critical thinking, the indirect effect, and its bootstrap interval are excluded; the indirect-effect interval must not be assigned to this total contrast. Figure 3 on PDF p. 7 has raster mediation-path labels inconsistent with the prose. Table 2 and the explicit total-effect sentence on PDF p. 6 supply the retained statistics; no figure-only number is recorded. Counts use the printed actual sample and per-group counts, not degrees of freedom; no exclusions or outcome-specific analyzed counts are separately reported. Both groups used ChatGPT while producing their scored AUT responses, supporting question=with_ai and outcome_with_ai=true. The design is between participants, so within_person=null. The averaged-rater creativity index is compared between people, supporting unit=participant, sd_level=participant, and se_basis=participant; the paper does not fully describe aggregation over individual ideas, rating dimensions, and the two AUT objects. The combined CAT index measures overall_creativity; higher scores indicate more_creative output. Expert-rater coding follows the trained psychology graduate raters and the description of the same measure as expert-rated on PDF p. 9. The contrast qualifies as ai_design because both arms use ChatGPT with different instructions. It also bundles different earlier priming experiences. High-dependence participants were instructed to adopt AI solutions directly, but people performed the task and submitted the scored responses, so this is not a model-only arm. The paper does not state the standardizer for Cohen’s d, and no SE or confidence interval is printed for the eligible overall contrast. All recorded numerical statistics are transcribed without calculation.

not_extracted.reason: No random assignment and no creativity scored on produced output. The questionnaire measures self-perceived creative capacity, not performance on a specific creative task (PDF p. 3, Sections 2.1-2.2; PDF p. 4, Section 2.3, Table 1 and Figure 2). Excluded under extraction rule 5.
Self-report manipulation check rather than an outcome scored on creative output (PDF p. 6, Sections 3.2-3.3 and Table 2).

Chinese Critical Thinking Structure Scale questionnaire, measured as in Study 1; not a scored-output creativity outcome or a convergent test with correct answers (PDF p. 3, Section 2.2, Measures; PDF p. 6, Sections 3.2-3.3 and Table 2).
Self-report alternative mediator, not a score on participants’ creative output (PDF p. 6, Section 3.2, Measures and Table 2).

not_extracted.reason: Mediation analyses and effects conditioned on post-treatment mediators are excluded under extraction rule 5. The printed total effect c is retained only as another statistic for the existing eligible full-sample creativity contrast; no mediation contrast or indirect-effect interval is extracted (PDF pp. 6-7, Section 3.3 and Figure 3).

not_extracted.what: S3 / S3-O1: High AI dependence, pooled over orientation, versus Low AI dependence, pooled over orientation (Table 4, Model 2)
not_extracted.reason: Deferred because random assignment to generative-AI assistance or differing generative-AI configurations cannot be confirmed. The described AI-dependence manipulation is an instruction about unnamed AI investment advice in a preliminary trust game. The subsequent AUT is called identical to Study 2, without specifying AI availability or condition-specific AI-use instructions. Consequently question, outcome_with_ai, and comparison_type cannot be assigned from the saved article. The supplementary task instructions were unavailable. This is a full-sample coefficient and is not excluded merely because Table 4 also reports moderation; the unresolved intervention prevents extraction under rule 4 (PDF pp. 7-8, Section 4.2; PDF p. 9, Table 4, Model 2; PDF p. 13, Supplementary Materials).

not_extracted.what: S3 / S3-O1: High AI dependence / outcome-oriented versus Low AI dependence / outcome-oriented, including the Table 4 Model 3 AI-dependence term
not_extracted.reason: Orientation-specific simple effect from the moderation analysis rather than a full-sample contrast; excluded under rules 4 and 5. Study 3 generative-AI assistance is also unresolved. The printed cell statistics and corresponding conditional regression term are not eligible estimates (PDF p. 9, Table 4, Model 3 and simple-effects paragraph; PDF pp. 9-10, orientation coding in the moderated-mediation analysis and Table 5).

not_extracted.what: S3 / S3-O1: High AI dependence / process-oriented versus Low AI dependence / process-oriented
not_extracted.reason: Orientation-specific simple effect from the moderation analysis rather than a full-sample contrast; excluded under rules 4 and 5. Study 3 generative-AI assistance is also unresolved (PDF p. 9, simple-effects paragraph below Table 4; intervention on PDF pp. 7-8, Section 4.2).

not_extracted.what: S3 / S3-O1: process orientation versus outcome orientation, pooled over AI dependence (Table 4, Model 2)
not_extracted.reason: This additional full-sample creativity coefficient was checked even though it is not a separate contrast in the screening form. The generative-AI conditions during the AUT remain unconfirmed, so it cannot be classified as an eligible comparison of AI configurations under rule 4. Table 4 Model 3 conditional orientation terms and the interaction are moderation results excluded under rule 5 (PDF pp. 7-8, Section 4.2; PDF p. 9, Table 4).

not_extracted.what: S3: AI-dependence and thinking-orientation manipulation checks; critical-thinking questionnaire and its regressions/simple effects
not_extracted.reason: Questionnaire measures, not creativity scored on produced output; the critical-thinking scale is not a convergent test with correct answers. Moderation analyses are additionally excluded under rule 5 (PDF p. 3, Section 2.2, Measures; PDF pp. 8-9, Section 4.3 and Table 3).

not_extracted.what: S3: conditional indirect effects and index of moderated mediation
not_extracted.reason: Mediation and moderation analyses excluded under rule 5, independently of unresolved Study 3 AI conditions (PDF pp. 9-10, Section 4.3, Moderated mediation model and Table 5).

open_items: Study 3 remains deferred: the supplementary task instructions are needed to establish whether generative AI was available during the AUT and whether AI use differed by randomized arm. The phrase identical to the AUT used in Study 2 does not specify those conditions. Identify the AI supplying trust-game advice and whether the low-dependence participants also saw that advice; the Study 3 setting is not explicitly described (PDF pp. 7-8, Section 4.2).

The supplementary materials listed on PDF p. 13 are not embedded in the PDF and the local supplement manifest lists no saved files. In this reconciliation, Python urllib requests with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 to https://www.mdpi.com/article/10.3390/jintelligence14080168/s1, https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC13514692/supplementaryFiles, and https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC13514692/fullTextXML all failed with WinError 10013 (socket access forbidden). No supplement contents were verified.
Study 2 does not name the ChatGPT model/version or its release year; ai_tool.year remains null (PDF pp. 5-6, Section 3.2).

The CAT procedure explains averaging raters but does not fully specify aggregation across AUT responses, objects, and rating dimensions. No separate dimension-level contrasts are printed in the saved article (PDF p. 6, Section 3.2, Measures and Table 2).

The standardizer for the printed Cohen’s d is not specified. No SE or confidence interval is printed for the eligible overall creativity contrast; arm means, SDs, and people counts are available (PDF pp. 5-6, Section 3.2 and Table 2).

The raster mediation-path labels in Figure 3 do not agree with the prose in Section 3.3. The extraction preserves the explicit prose total effect and Table 2 statistics without substituting or calculating any number from the figure (PDF pp. 6-7).

If Study 3 eligibility is later established, its cell-level analyzed counts and reported simple-effect statistics still require clarification. Cell-specific analyzed counts are not printed and the outcome-oriented test degrees of freedom are inconsistent with the randomized cell sizes. These conditional contrasts remain excluded under the present full-sample extraction rules (PDF p. 7, Section 4.2; PDF p. 9, simple-effects paragraph).
notes: Reconciled on 2026-10-10. Read extraction-spec.md and the creativity codebook before reviewing the candidate record, retrieval record, citation record, screening form and final.open_items, both raw extractions, and their diff. Read the complete markdown conversion in consecutive chunks, including end matter and all references. The saved PDF contains no appendix or embedded supplement. Every cited PDF page was checked with pymupdf; Table 2 is legible in the extracted PDF text, and the Figure 3 raster was inspected in memory. Only S2 meets the extraction criteria on confirmed information. S1-O1 and all three screening contrasts of S3-O1 are explicitly accounted for in not_extracted, along with the additional full-sample orientation coefficient in Study 3 and unreported separate CAT dimensions. No eligible estimate is present in only one extractor: only_in_a and only_in_b are empty. No eligible outcome or contrast missed by both was confirmed, so no estimate was added. A’s slug is retained as the canonical identifier; the matched B slug refers to the same contrast. The ai_tool wording difference is resolved to A, and the printed total effect is retained from B with its meaning stated explicitly. Shared counts, question, construct, unit, higher_is, outcome_with_ai, within_person, and comparison_type were checked independently against the PDF rather than accepted on agreement. Randomization and the actual sample statement on PDF p. 5 support the people counts. The laboratory procedure and explicit ChatGPT-use instructions on PDF pp. 5-6 support the design and AI availability; CAT scoring and participant comparisons on PDF p. 6 support the outcome coding. The country is China, supported by the institution description on PDF p. 3 and the statement that all participants came from a single institution on PDF p. 12. Preregistration is not stated in the saved article. The form identifies no shared participant sample with another paper; possible participation across this paper’s studies is not described. No diversity or delayed unassisted creativity outcome is reported. No sample size, mean difference, effect size, SD, SE, or interval was calculated; original numerical precision is preserved in the source quotes.

Its location in a mediation paragraph does not change the estimand. Rule 5 excludes the mediation paths, mediator-adjusted direct effect, and indirect effect; none is extracted.
